moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Use local debugging controls, helper panels, supported browser JavaScript debugging and positioned recording.
Pause, continue, and step through a running test to inspect its behavior.
Distinguish manual breakpoints from virtual breakpoints.

elements.title: Testim Debugging Tools
items: Debug controls pause and step through local debug runs; normal local runs ignore breakpoints.
Helper panels expose logs, breakpoint locations and parameters from executed steps.
Supported browser JavaScript steps can be inspected through Chrome DevTools; this is not a general Node.js CLI debugger.
Positioned recording adds steps after establishing the required application state.

elements.text: Use the available evidence to investigate a failure. These tools do not guarantee an exact root cause or turn an application defect into a test defect.

bulletPoints: Local debug mode differs from normal execution.
Inspect evidence before changing the test.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Debugging Helper Panels and JS Code Debugging

elements.description: Console Log filters messages and can preserve them between runs; Breakpoint Manager locates/removes breakpoints; Scope shows incoming parameters and test/global exports. Future, unexecuted steps have no runtime values to inspect.

For supported browser steps, pause before the step in a local debug run, use Step Into, switch to the AUT, open Chrome DevTools and follow the confirmation prompt. Inspect the code, resume its execution and return to the editor. Supported types include custom action/validation/wait, email/network validation and API action/validation; CLI actions are not listed for this browser workflow.

bulletPoints: Scope is evidence from executed steps, not values from future steps.
Chrome DevTools inspects supported code running in the AUT browser, rather than all Node.js CLI code.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Debugging Controls: pausing and stepping through a test

elements.description: Pause stops at the nearest step boundary in local debug mode. Continue proceeds from the current location; another breakpoint can pause it again.

Start a local run with debugging. Pause or insert a breakpoint, then use the available stepping controls. Step Over executes a step/group; Step Into opens a group before its first step; Step Out executes its remaining steps before leaving.

Breakpoints pause execution at various stages. Manual breakpoints are explicitly set by the user at a chosen step. Virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system when debugging controls are used — such as step into, step out, step over, and pause — without the user having to set them by hand.

elements.text: Breakpoint Manager identifies breakpoint locations, supports navigation and removal, and highlights the current pause.

bulletPoints: Continue resumes; a later breakpoint can stop the run again.
Step Over executes the group; Step Into opens it; Step Out executes the remainder.
Manual breakpoints are user placed; virtual markers arise from debugging controls.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming all breakpoints must be manually placed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Not realizing that using debugging controls like step into/out/over automatically creates breakpoints of their own.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system whenever debugging controls (step into, step out, step over, pause) are used — they exist alongside any manual breakpoints you set yourself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the difference between a manual breakpoint and a virtual breakpoint?

options.text: There is no difference — they are the same thing.
Manual breakpoints are set explicitly by the user; virtual breakpoints are created automatically when debugging controls are used.
Manual breakpoints only work in production; virtual breakpoints only work locally.
Virtual breakpoints can only be set on API steps.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is placed by hand, the other appears as a side effect of using debugging tools.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Manual breakpoints are set by the user; virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system when debugging controls (step into, step out, step over, pause) are used.

optionExplanations.A: Manual and virtual markers have different origins.
optionExplanations.B: Manual markers are user placed; virtual markers are created by debug controls.
optionExplanations.C: These are local debugging concepts, not a production/local split.
optionExplanations.D: Virtual markers are not limited to API steps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which workflow allows controlled inspection of steps in the current Testim editor?

options.text: Run locally with debugging, pause or use a breakpoint, and use stepping controls.
This is not supported — tests always run start to finish.
Delete all steps except the one you want to inspect.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Local debug mode exposes stepping controls. A normal local run ignores breakpoints; deletion or a zero timeout is not a debugging workflow.

optionExplanations.B: Local debug mode supports controlled execution.
optionExplanations.C: Deleting steps changes coverage rather than providing inspection.
optionExplanations.D: Zero timeout does not enable debugging.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After clicking Pause during a test run, what does clicking Continue do?

options.text: Restarts the entire test from the first step.
Continues from the paused location; another breakpoint can pause the run again.
Skips the remainder of the test entirely.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Continue resumes execution at the current location, subject to later breakpoints; it does not restart or skip all remaining steps.

optionExplanations.A: Rerun, rather than Continue, restarts the test.
optionExplanations.B: Continue resumes; later breakpoints may pause again.
optionExplanations.C: Continue executes remaining work rather than discarding it.
optionExplanations.D: Continue is an execution control, not a locator-panel command.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A failure is isolated to a supported browser custom validation. Which workflow can inspect its JavaScript code?

options.text: Debugging Controls again, since it covers everything.
Recording New Steps to Resolve Bugs.

practiceQuiz.hint: The code runs in the AUT browser.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Step Into from a breakpoint before a supported step leads to Chrome DevTools in the AUT. This workflow does not establish support for Node.js CLI steps.

optionExplanations.A: Step-level controls alone do not expose source-level browser inspection.
optionExplanations.B: The supported browser JS workflow uses Chrome DevTools in the AUT.
optionExplanations.C: Recording adds steps rather than diagnosing existing code.
optionExplanations.D: Result labels annotate runs rather than stepping through code.

quickRecap.value: Local controls, helper panels, supported browser JS debugging and positioned recording have distinct roles.
Pause stops at a nearby step boundary; Continue resumes until another pause or completion.
Local debug mode exposes Step Over, Step Into and Step Out; normal local runs ignore breakpoints.
Auto-created by debugging controls (step into/out/over, pause).
